passage:
Zubin: Bro, Uncle says you turned down the supervisor post at the workshop??
Thomas: Yeah.
Zubin: WHY. More money. Your own team.
Thomas: I'd spend all day on schedules. I'd stop making things.
Zubin: So you'll be an apprentice forever? Everyone thinks you've got no ambition.
Thomas: I have a plan. It's just not loud.
Thomas: I want to cut a dovetail joint by hand so tight it doesn't need glue. Right now mine still have gaps.
Zubin: That's the goal?
Thomas: For this year. Next year, chairs that don't wobble after ten years.
Zubin: Okay, that's actually kind of intense.
Thomas: 🙂 it is to me.
Zubin: Send me a photo when the joint's perfect.
Thomas: You'll be the first.

qa.q: What post did Thomas turn down at the workshop?
qa.a: The supervisor post at the workshop.

qa.q: Why did Thomas turn down the post, and what does it show about what Thomas wants?
qa.a: Thomas didn't want to spend all day on schedules and stop making things; it shows Thomas wants deep skill in the craft more than a title.

qa.q: What choice did Thomas make when told everyone thinks there is no ambition?
qa.a: Thomas chose to share the quiet plan, a glue-free dovetail and chairs that last, which turned Zubin from doubting to curious.

qa.q: How did Zubin's view of Thomas change during the chat?
qa.a: Zubin began by seeing a lack of drive, then found the goal intense and asked for a photo of the perfect joint.

grounding: Shows a young adult who cares more about mastering a craft than about a title, with private steady goals that others misread as lacking drive.

passage:
Every evening after the kiln cooled, Kalyani stayed back in her uncle's pottery shed at the edge of the kasba and threw the same water pot, again and again. Thin walls, even rim. She crushed most of them back into clay.
Mridul, who had joined the shed the same year, was already selling his own designs at the Tuesday market and talking about opening a shop on the highway.
'You'll be making pots for your uncle till you're old,' he said, washing up. 'Don't you want anything?'
Kalyani pressed her thumb into the spinning clay. 'I want this rim to be the same thickness all the way round.'
He laughed. She didn't mind. Last week the old potter from the next village had picked up one of her pots, tapped it, listened to the ring and nodded once.

qa.q: What pot did Kalyani throw again and again?
qa.a: The same water pot, with thin walls and an even rim.

qa.q: What does Kalyani crushing most pots back into clay show about what she wants?
qa.a: It shows she wants true skill more than quick sales, holding herself to a standard others can't see.

qa.q: What moment showed Kalyani that her private practice was paying off?
qa.a: The old potter tapping her pot, listening to its ring and nodding once was quiet recognition from someone who knows the craft.

qa.q: How does Mridul read Kalyani's quiet evenings in the shed?
qa.a: Mridul reads them as a lack of ambition, since for him drive means selling designs and opening a shop.

grounding: Shows a young adult quietly working to master a craft rather than chase status, whose private goals a peer misreads as lack of drive.
